---
title: "Native histogram trainer"
---

The default duckboost trainer is a **dependency-free histogram GBDT**. Pass `backend = 'native'` (or the compatible alias `'reference'`). Model JSON still stores `"backend":"reference"` so older dumps keep loading.

This page walks through a realistic SQL path — categoricals, early stopping, feature importance, SQL export — then publishes small holdout benchmarks against the optional in-process LightGBM backend when it is linked.

## What the native trainer does

| Capability | Option / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Global quantile bins | `max_bins` (default 256); thresholds fixed once from training rows |
| Categoricals | `categorical_features`: ordered `g/h` partitions → `EQUAL` or `IN` |
| Growth | `growth_policy`: `depthwise` (default), `lossguide`, `oblivious` / `symmetric` (all score continuous splits from the same global bins) |
| Losses | squared / absolute / quantile / expectile; binary logistic; multiclass softmax |
| Regularization | `reg_lambda`, `reg_alpha`, `min_split_gain` (`gamma`) |
| Sampling | `subsample`, `colsample_bytree`, `class_weight`, `seed` |
| Early stopping | `early_stopping_rounds` + `validation_fraction`, or a BOOLEAN `is_validation` column |
| Missing values | Feature `NULL` → NaN; per-split `default_left` |

Limits to keep in mind: single-threaded, materializes all training rows, no monotonic constraints or CatBoost CTRs. See [Use cases](../use-cases.qmd).

## End-to-end: penguins with a categorical

Encode island as an integer category, mark it categorical, hold out 20% for early stopping, then inspect importance and export SQL.

```sql
LOAD duckboost;
CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS y,
  bill_length_mm::DOUBLE AS bill_length_mm,
  bill_depth_mm::DOUBLE AS bill_depth_mm,
  flipper_length_mm::DOUBLE AS flipper_length_mm,
  CASE island
    WHEN 'Biscoe' THEN 0.0
    WHEN 'Dream' THEN 1.0
    WHEN 'Torgersen' THEN 2.0
  END AS island_id
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_depth_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND flipper_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND island IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, island_id],
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '80',
    'max_depth': '4',
    'learning_rate': '0.1',
    'min_samples_leaf': '5',
    'reg_lambda': '1.0',
    'early_stopping_rounds': '8',
    'validation_fraction': '0.2',
    'seed': '42',
    'feature_names': 'bill_length_mm,bill_depth_mm,flipper_length_mm,island',
    'categorical_features': 'island'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins;

SELECT
  model LIKE '%"backend":"reference"%' AS json_backend_reference,
  length(regexp_extract_all(model, '"is_leaf":false')) AS n_splits,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(
    model, y,
    [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, island_id],
    MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}
  ), 1) AS training_rmse_g
FROM models, penguins
GROUP BY model;

SET VARIABLE native_model = (SELECT model FROM models);
SELECT variable, round(importance, 3) AS importance, frequency
FROM duckboost_importance(getvariable('native_model'))
ORDER BY importance DESC;
```

```text
┌────────────────────────┬──────────┬─────────────────┐
│ json_backend_reference │ n_splits │ training_rmse_g │
├────────────────────────┼──────────┼─────────────────┤
│ true                   │ 342      │ 275.4           │
└────────────────────────┴──────────┴─────────────────┘
┌───────────────────┬────────────┬───────────┐
│     variable      │ importance │ frequency │
├───────────────────┼────────────┼───────────┤
│ flipper_length_mm │ 0.859      │ 90        │
│ bill_depth_mm     │ 0.079      │ 134       │
│ bill_length_mm    │ 0.053      │ 100       │
│ island            │ 0.009      │ 18        │
└───────────────────┴────────────┴───────────┘
```


Export for scoring without calling the extension:

```sql
LOAD duckboost;
CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS y,
  bill_length_mm::DOUBLE AS bill_length_mm,
  bill_depth_mm::DOUBLE AS bill_depth_mm,
  flipper_length_mm::DOUBLE AS flipper_length_mm,
  CASE island
    WHEN 'Biscoe' THEN 0.0
    WHEN 'Dream' THEN 1.0
    WHEN 'Torgersen' THEN 2.0
  END AS island_id
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_depth_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND flipper_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND island IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, island_id],
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '20',
    'max_depth': '3',
    'learning_rate': '0.15',
    'feature_names': 'bill_length_mm,bill_depth_mm,flipper_length_mm,island',
    'categorical_features': 'island'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins;

SELECT left(sql, 120) AS sql_prefix
FROM (
  SELECT duckboost_to_sql(
    model,
    'penguins',
    ['bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm', 'flipper_length_mm', 'island_id'],
    MAP {'separate_trees': 'false', 'prediction_alias': 'pred', 'keep_columns': 'y'}
  ) AS sql
  FROM models
);
```



## Oblivious trees

CatBoost-style symmetric growth shares one split definition per depth. Useful when you want a compact, regular tree shape.

```sql
LOAD duckboost;
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT
  (i % 7)::DOUBLE AS x1,
  (i % 5)::DOUBLE AS x2,
  ((i % 7) + 0.5 * (i % 5))::DOUBLE AS y
FROM range(200) t(i);

CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x1, x2],
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'growth_policy': 'oblivious',
    'n_estimators': '15',
    'max_depth': '3',
    'learning_rate': '0.2',
    'min_samples_leaf': '4'
  }
) AS model
FROM train;

SELECT
  length(regexp_extract_all(model, '"is_leaf":false')) AS internal_nodes,
  length(regexp_extract_all(model, '"is_leaf":true')) AS leaves,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(model, y, [x1, x2], MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}), 3) AS rmse
FROM models, train
GROUP BY model;
```

```text
┌────────────────┬────────┬───────┐
│ internal_nodes │ leaves │ rmse  │
├────────────────┼────────┼───────┤
│ 105            │ 120    │ 0.156 │
└────────────────┴────────┴───────┘
```


## Published benchmarks

Holdout metrics on two repository CSVs. Splits are deterministic (hash of the feature vector + seed) so numbers are stable across renders. When this binary has LightGBM linked, the same grid is also trained with `backend = 'lightgbm'` for a side-by-side check — not a claim that native wins every time.

```sql
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE iris AS
SELECT
  (species = 'setosa')::DOUBLE AS y,
  [sepal_length, sepal_width, petal_length, petal_width] AS features,
  hash(sepal_length, sepal_width, petal_length, petal_width, 7) AS h
FROM (
SELECT
  "Sepal.Length" AS sepal_length,
  "Sepal.Width" AS sepal_width,
  "Petal.Length" AS petal_length,
  "Petal.Width" AS petal_width,
  Species AS species
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vincentarelbundock/Rdatasets/master/csv/datasets/iris.csv')
);

CREATE TABLE iris_split AS
SELECT *, CASE WHEN h % 5 = 0 THEN 'test' ELSE 'train' END AS split
FROM iris;

CREATE TABLE iris_native AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'task': 'binary',
    'n_estimators': '40',
    'max_depth': '3',
    'learning_rate': '0.2',
    'min_samples_leaf': '2',
    'seed': '7'
  }
) AS model
FROM iris_split WHERE split = 'train';

SELECT
  'iris-setosa' AS problem,
  'native' AS trainer,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(m.model, t.y, t.features, MAP {'metric': 'accuracy'}), 3) AS holdout_metric,
  'accuracy' AS metric
FROM iris_native m, iris_split t
WHERE t.split = 'test';
```

```text
┌─────────────┬─────────┬────────────────┬──────────┐
│   problem   │ trainer │ holdout_metric │  metric  │
├─────────────┼─────────┼────────────────┼──────────┤
│ iris-setosa │ native  │ 1.0            │ accuracy │
└─────────────┴─────────┴────────────────┴──────────┘
```


```sql
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS y,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, (sex = 'male')::DOUBLE] AS features,
  hash(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, sex, 11) AS h
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND sex IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE penguins_split AS
SELECT *, CASE WHEN h % 5 = 0 THEN 'test' ELSE 'train' END AS split
FROM penguins;

CREATE TABLE penguins_native AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '60',
    'max_depth': '4',
    'learning_rate': '0.1',
    'min_samples_leaf': '4',
    'reg_lambda': '1.0',
    'seed': '11'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins_split WHERE split = 'train';

SELECT
  'penguins-body-mass' AS problem,
  'native' AS trainer,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(m.model, t.y, t.features, MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}), 1) AS holdout_metric,
  'rmse_g' AS metric
FROM penguins_native m, penguins_split t
WHERE t.split = 'test';
```

```text
┌────────────────────┬─────────┬────────────────┬────────┐
│      problem       │ trainer │ holdout_metric │ metric │
├────────────────────┼─────────┼────────────────┼────────┤
│ penguins-body-mass │ native  │ 322.7          │ rmse_g │
└────────────────────┴─────────┴────────────────┴────────┘
```


Optional LightGBM comparison (skipped automatically when that backend is not linked):

```sql
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE penguins AS
SELECT
  body_mass_g::DOUBLE AS y,
  [bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, (sex = 'male')::DOUBLE] AS features,
  hash(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, sex, 11) AS h
FROM read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/master/inst/extdata/penguins.csv', nullstr = 'NA')
WHERE body_mass_g IS NOT NULL
  AND bill_length_mm IS NOT NULL
  AND sex IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE penguins_split AS
SELECT *, CASE WHEN h % 5 = 0 THEN 'test' ELSE 'train' END AS split
FROM penguins;

CREATE TABLE trainer_models AS
SELECT 'native' AS trainer, duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'native',
    'n_estimators': '60',
    'max_depth': '4',
    'learning_rate': '0.1',
    'min_samples_leaf': '4',
    'reg_lambda': '1.0',
    'seed': '11'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins_split WHERE split = 'train'
UNION ALL
SELECT 'lightgbm' AS trainer, duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {
    'backend': 'lightgbm',
    'n_estimators': '60',
    'max_depth': '4',
    'learning_rate': '0.1',
    'min_samples_leaf': '4',
    'seed': '11'
  }
) AS model
FROM penguins_split WHERE split = 'train';

SELECT
  b.trainer,
  round(duckboost_evaluate_agg(b.model, t.y, t.features, MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}), 1) AS holdout_rmse_g
FROM trainer_models b, penguins_split t
WHERE t.split = 'test'
GROUP BY b.trainer, b.model
ORDER BY b.trainer;
```

```text
┌──────────┬────────────────┐
│ trainer  │ holdout_rmse_g │
├──────────┼────────────────┤
│ lightgbm │ 312.1          │
│ native   │ 322.7          │
└──────────┴────────────────┘
```


These figures are **smoke-level evidence**, not a bake-off. They show the native trainer learns useful structure on the shipped CSVs and stays in the same ballpark as LightGBM under a small shared grid when that backend is available.

For a larger (~200k row) synthetic holdout with wall times, see the [Native vs LightGBM benchmark](../benchmarks.qmd) page (`scripts/native_benchmark/run.py`).
